findings.issue_text: [BUG] CreateOrUpdateDevice calls s.CountDevices(ctx, time.Now().UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration), time.Now().UTC().Add(time.Minute)) passing time.Time values, but the store's CountDevices is declared as CountDevices(ctx context.Context, from *time.Time, to *time.Time) (int64, error) — the same pointer signature as ListDevices, whose declaration is visible in this diff's own hunk header — so the package does not compile. Build failure: "cannot use time.Now().UTC().Add(...) (value of type time.Time) as *time.Time value in argument to s.CountDevices" — the anonstore package, its tests, and every dependent (anonimpl service, authn anonymous client) fail to compile, so the PR cannot build or pass CI.

[BUG] The new limit-reached path does `return nil, err` where err is a plain error, but Anonymous.Authenticate implements authn.Client (asserted by `var _ authn.ContextAwareClient = new(Anonymous)`) and is declared to return (*authn.Identity, *authn.Error), which a bare error does not satisfy. Build failure: "cannot use err (variable of type error) as *authn.Error value in return statement" — anonimpl does not compile; the repo's contract for client failures is a constructed &authn.Error{Status: ..., Message: ...}, so even the intended behavior (rejecting over-limit devices with a real HTTP status) is unimplemented.

[BUG] Both wire providers change signature — ProvideAnonymousDeviceService replaces its anonstore.AnonStore parameter with db.DB, and anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore gains a deviceLimit int64 — but the diff updates no production wiring: Grafana constructs these services through the checked-in google/wire output (pkg/server/wire_gen.go, fed by the provider set in pkg/server/wire.go), which still calls anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(db) with one argument and passes the resulting *AnonDBStore into the db.DB parameter slot of ProvideAnonymousDeviceService. The server target does not build: "not enough arguments in call to anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore" and "cannot use anonDBStore (variable of type *anonstore.AnonDBStore) as db.DB value" at the generated call sites; wire additionally has no provider for a bare int64, so the wire set itself must be edited (ProvideAnonDBStore removed from the graph) and wire_gen.go regenerated — neither file appears in this diff.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice is moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine (context.Background with a dedicated 2-minute timeout and recover) onto the synchronous authentication path, so anonymous authn now performs the anon_device COUNT plus INSERT/UPDATE inline in the request. Operators of anonymous-access instances (public dashboards, demos) get anonymous page-load latency coupled to database I/O on every localCache miss (first request per device per 29-minute window): a slow or saturated DB now stalls anonymous authentication where tagging previously never delayed a response, and the dedicated 2-minute timeout is gone, so a hung DB call holds the request until the client disconnects.

[ADVISORY] The device limit is enforced with a non-transactional count-then-act sequence: CountDevices and the subsequent insert run as separate statements with no row lock, transaction, or cross-instance coordination. Operators who set device_limit expecting a hard cap see it exceeded under burst traffic: N distinct devices arriving concurrently while count is at limit-1 all read count < limit and all insert (multi-instance HA deployments widen the window), and nothing later trims the excess because the cleanup job only deletes rows older than 61 days.

[ADVISORY] The new TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit covers only the rejection branch of the limit path (updateDevice matches 0 rows → ErrDeviceLimitReached); no test in the diff exercises the success branch where an existing device at capacity is updated (rowsAffected == 1 → nil). A regression in updateDevice's WHERE window or argument order (e.g., swapping the two BETWEEN time bounds, which yields 0 rows affected) rejects every anonymous request once the limit is reached — a full anonymous-access outage — while the integration suite stays green.

[ADVISORY] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit covers only the rejection branch of the new limit logic — a second new device over the limit returns ErrDeviceLimitReached — and no test in the diff exercises updateDevice's success path, i.e. that an existing recently-active device is admitted and refreshed when the limit is reached. A regression in updateDevice (database.go:73-103), such as inverted BETWEEN bounds or misordered arguments, fails every returning device once the limit is reached — a total anonymous-access outage — while the diff's test suite stays green, because the feature's core acceptance criterion (returning devices keep working at the limit) has no verification anywhere in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The diff sets no acceptance criterion and adds no test for what an over-limit anonymous user actually receives: Authenticate returns the bare anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached, leaving status code and message to authn's generic error mapping, and the anonymousDeviceLimit value shipped to the frontend is read by no frontend code in the diff. Over-limit users get an unspecified generic auth failure with no device-limit explanation — the exact status depends on authn's default error mapping, which no test pins, so it can silently change in a refactor — and operators have no defined user-facing behavior for the feature's defining event.

[BUG] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit with an unguarded check-then-act sequence — CountDevices in one DB session followed by the insert in a separate session, with no transaction, row lock, or admission guard — so concurrent first-time requests all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert. Simultaneous anonymous requests overshoot the configured limit (a limit of 1 admits 2 or more devices under two concurrent requests), so the cap this PR exists to deliver is violated under precisely the concurrent anonymous traffic (bots, shared NAT, cookie-less crawlers) the feature targets, and no test in the diff covers concurrent admission.

[ADVISORY] Tagging moved from a background goroutine (context.Background with a 2-minute timeout and a recover() panic net) onto the synchronous request path with no replacement mitigations: the DB call now uses the deadline-less request context, rejected devices get no negative-result caching, and the panic recovery is deleted. With a limit configured, every cache-miss anonymous request blocks on a new CountDevices query plus the write — two synchronous DB round-trips per request for cookie-less clients that never reuse the 29-minute local cache — a slow or wedged DB hangs anonymous page loads until the client disconnects, and a panic in the tagging path now fails the request outright instead of being logged.

[ADVISORY] The limit treats every cookie-less request as a brand-new device, and the diff contains no acceptance criterion or test for legitimate cookie-less internal clients — the image renderer fetching /render endpoints for alert notification images, health probes, and embedded dashboards — that present a fresh device_id per request. Once the configured limit fills, the renderer's next per-request fresh device is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the render request fails authentication, and alert notification images break — an outage of legitimate infrastructure unrelated to the abusive traffic the limit targets, unacknowledged anywhere in the diff.

[ADVISORY] A device-limit rejection produces no log at the default level: TagDevice records it only via a.log.Debug before returning, and client.go's Warn-level 'Failed to tag anonymous session' is skipped because the errors.Is(ErrDeviceLimitReached) branch returns first. Operators running at the default Info level get no log line and no metric when the limit starts refusing anonymous users, so a limit-induced drop in anonymous traffic is indistinguishable from a broken anonymous-auth setup until debug logging is enabled.

[ADVISORY] The 30-day device lifetime constant now exists twice — anonymousDeviceExpiration in api.go and a separate identically-valued anonymousDeviceExpiration in anonstore/database.go — instead of one shared definition. The admin ListDevices window and the store's limit/expiry window silently diverge the next time one constant is edited (e.g. the store moves to a 60-day lifetime while the admin device list still shows a 30-day window), and neither package gets a compile-time signal about the other.

[ADVISORY] The config reader parses auth.anonymous device_limit but the diff adds no device_limit entry to the shipped conf/defaults.ini template, breaking the pattern of every sibling auth.anonymous key (enabled, org_name, org_role, hide_version). Operators who configure Grafana from the documented defaults.ini never discover the option, so the feature ships hidden and is reachable only by readers of the source code.

[ADVISORY] ProvideAnonymousDeviceService replaced the injectable anonstore.AnonStore parameter with db.DB and hardcodes anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit) internally, deleting the only seam for substituting the store in tests. AnonDeviceService and its API can no longer be tested with a fake store — the diff's own impl_test.go had to be rewritten to seed a real test database — so future service-level tests of limit behavior (e.g. simulating ErrDeviceLimitReached without standing up a DB) have no injection point.

[BUG] The diff changes the exported signatures of ProvideAnonymousDeviceService (anonstore.AnonStore parameter replaced with db.DB) and anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore (new required deviceLimit int64) but contains no update to the production wiring that constructs this service — the wire-generated call site in pkg/server/wire_gen.go and the anonstore provider-set registration — so the tree as diffed does not compile. The unchanged generated wiring still calls the old signatures and the build fails; additionally, wire codegen cannot synthesize a bare int64 argument, so ProvideAnonDBStore must be dropped from or rewritten in the provider set, and none of that required work appears in this diff.

[BUG] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the device limit with a CountDevices read followed by a separate, non-transactional insert/update, so the configured cap is not actually enforced under concurrency. Two concurrent first-visit requests (or several pods with cold local caches) each read count < deviceLimit and each insert, so the active-device count exceeds the configured limit — an attacker scripting cookie-less requests races past the cap, and the feature's core invariant (at most device_limit active devices) silently fails.

[BUG] Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context with no timeout, replacing the background goroutine that was capped at 2 minutes and never blocked authentication. Every cache-miss anonymous request (first visit per device per 29-minute window per pod, and every request while a pod's local cache is cold after a restart) blocks on a database round-trip with no bound — a slow or down database hangs anonymous page loads until the client gives up, where previously tagging failures only produced a warning and auth always proceeded.

[ADVISORY] The only new test (TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit) exercises updateDevice's zero-row rejection branch, leaving the branch that keeps an existing active device working at the limit — and the client.Authenticate rejection path — with no coverage in the diff. A regression in updateDevice's BETWEEN window (database.go:80-81) or in the errors.Is dispatch in client.go silently locks out every active anonymous device the moment the limit is reached — the worst-case outcome of this feature — and no test in the diff fails to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The diff plumbs anonymousDeviceLimit through FrontendSettingsDTO, getFrontendSettings, GrafanaBootConfig, and the GrafanaConfig interface but ships no frontend code that reads it, making the field dead payload on a public endpoint. Every unauthenticated visitor receives the operator's configured device limit in the public frontend-settings payload with nothing consuming it, and the limit-reached failure the value was presumably meant to explain is never rendered — rejected users get an unexplained generic error.

[ADVISORY] The rewrite deletes the recover() that deliberately guarded the tagging path, so a panic inside TagDevice or the anon store now propagates out of Authenticate instead of being logged and skipped. A panic in device tagging — the exact failure the removed 'Tag anon session panic' handler was added to contain — now fails the entire anonymous request with a 500 rather than degrading to a warning, a safety-net removal not traceable to the device-limit requirement.

[ADVISORY] When the limit is reached, Authenticate returns the bare sentinel anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached with no mapping to an HTTP status, error class, or user-facing message anywhere in the diff. A rejected device receives whatever generic auth-failure response the middleware produces — indistinguishable from an internal malfunction for the user — and enforcement shows up in logs and error metrics as an ordinary auth error, so operators cannot tell deliberate rejections apart from bugs.

[ADVISORY] ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now constructs the concrete AnonDBStore internally instead of receiving the anonstore.AnonStore interface — a refactor the device-limit requirement does not demand, since a wire provider binding cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit to an AnonStore preserves the injection seam. The only injection point for store implementations is deleted: future service-level tests of the limit logic are forced onto a real SQL database, and any alternate or fake AnonStore is cut off even though the interface remains exported and is still accepted by the API constructor.

[BUG] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the device limit with an unserialized count-then-insert (TOCTOU): concurrent requests each observe count < deviceLimit and each insert, so the limit is not enforced under exactly the concurrent load it exists to cap. A burst of concurrent new anonymous visitors (viral link, bot flood) overshoots the configured cap by an unbounded number of rows because there is no transaction, lock, or constraint serializing the CountDevices check against the insert; the excess rows then hold active slots for up to 30 days, during which every genuinely new device is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached — a momentary race converts into a sustained lockout of new anonymous users.

[BUG] Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context with no timeout, replacing the previous background goroutine that was bounded by a 2-minute timeout, so anonymous authentication blocks on the anon_device database with no bound. Every cache-miss anonymous request now waits for a COUNT plus an INSERT/UPDATE roundtrip before authentication completes, and a hung or slow database (lock contention, network partition) stalls anonymous auth indefinitely instead of degrading to untracked anonymous access — the removed timeoutTag was the only bound on this dependency, and the request context provides none.

[BUG] ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned from the authn client as a bare error with no HTTP status attached, so the auth layer surfaces a deliberate policy rejection as an undifferentiated server error rather than a 4xx. Anonymous users beyond the configured limit receive a generic 500 Internal Server Error on every request instead of a deliberate auth failure, and operators get server-fault alert noise for what is a configured policy decision, not a malfunction.

[ADVISORY] The rejection path has no negative caching: ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned before tagDeviceUI populates its 29-minute local cache (the cache Put only happens on success), so a rejected device re-runs CountDevices plus the failed UPDATE on every single request. Once the limit is reached — the feature's steady operating state — every page refresh from every rejected anonymous user synchronously drives an O(active-devices) COUNT over the 30-day window (a full-table scan if updated_at is unindexed) plus an UPDATE attempt through the auth path, so database load peaks exactly when the cap is active and compounds the latency regression on the same critical path.

[ADVISORY] The enforced limit counts hashed (client IP, user-agent) pairs — the pre-existing best-effort usage-stats device identity — so this diff turns a known-fuzzy heuristic into an access-control gate. Mobile/CGNAT users whose IPs rotate mint a fresh device per IP change and exhaust the cap (locking themselves and subsequent users out), while thousands of users behind one corporate proxy share a single slot — once the limit is reached the 'device limit' denies humans rather than devices, a consequence the config name does not signal to the operator setting it.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice's error contract changed from log-and-swallow to propagate, but the diff updates only the authn client caller; the renderer-path TagDevice caller (AnonDeviceRenderer) was written against the old best-effort contract and now receives store errors it was never designed to handle. If the rendering service's caller propagates the returned error, dashboard rendering and refresh for anonymous sessions fail whenever the device limit is reached or the store errors — a caller this diff never audited, hit precisely when the new limit is active.

[ADVISORY] The 30-day anonymous device expiration is now defined twice — anonymousDeviceExpiration here and an independent anonymousDeviceExpiration in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go:17 — with no compile-time link between the copies. The store's limit-count and update-eligibility windows and the admin device-list window silently diverge on the next edit (extending retention to 60 days in the store leaves the API listing only 30 days of devices), and the next editor cannot tell the two same-named constants are meant to move together.

[ADVISORY] The only new test covers the rejection path; updateDevice's success path (rowsAffected = 1, an existing device refreshed while the limit is reached) is exercised by no test in the diff. A regression in updateDevice's WHERE window (wrong column or wrong bound) would reject every previously-active anonymous device with ErrDeviceLimitReached once the limit is reached — the exact users the design intends to keep — and every test in this diff stays green.

[BUG] Replacing the background goroutine with a synchronous TagDevice call deletes the recover() that previously isolated tagging panics, so a panic anywhere in the tagging path now propagates out of Anonymous.Authenticate. An anonymous visitor whose request triggers a panic in TagDevice receives a 500 from the global panic-recovery middleware instead of a successful page load plus a warning log — the exact failure mode the deleted recover() (log message 'Tag anon session panic') was added to absorb.

[ADVISORY] Tagging was moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine (detached context, 2-minute timeout) onto the synchronous authentication path for all anonymous traffic, including deployments that never configure device_limit (default 0). Every cache-miss anonymous request now blocks Authenticate on a database roundtrip, so a degraded or slow database stalls anonymous page loads that previously never waited for tagging; the accepted objective was an opt-in configurable limit, but every existing anonymous-enabled deployment inherits the latency and failure coupling of the enforcement mechanism whether or not they enable it.

[ADVISORY] Once the device limit is saturated, every request from an unknown device executes the CountDevices range query plus a failing UPDATE synchronously, and because rejected devices are never tagged they never enter the 29-minute local cache, so each retry repeats the full database pair with no backoff. A saturated instance with device_limit set performs two database queries per anonymous request precisely for the traffic it is rejecting; a burst of new anonymous visitors (viral link, crawler, shared NAT) amplifies database load at the worst moment, now on the blocking auth path.

[ADVISORY] The ErrDeviceLimitReached branch returns the bare sentinel with no logging, no HTTP status mapping, and no metric, and no other component in the codebase knows this newly introduced sentinel. Operators who enable device_limit see anonymous users denied through the generic authentication-failure path — the sibling error branch logs a warning while this one stays silent — so limit rejections are indistinguishable from real auth failures during incident triage, and denied users get an opaque error with no indication the limit is the cause.

[ADVISORY] The limit is enforced as a non-atomic check-then-act: CountDevices and the subsequent insert run as separate statements with no transaction, row lock, or constraint backing the cap. Concurrent first requests from more new devices than remaining capacity all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert, so burst traffic overshoots the configured limit; an operator using device_limit as a hard compliance or licensing cap gets a soft cap instead.

[ADVISORY] The diff introduces a second independent copy of the 30-day expiration constant (anonymousDeviceExpiration here and in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go:18) instead of sharing one source of truth. A future retention change edited in only one package silently desynchronizes the admin device-list window (api.go ListDevices) from the limit-enforcement window (CreateOrUpdateDevice/updateDevice), so operators see devices listed that the limiter treats as expired — or active devices missing from the admin list.

[ADVISORY] updateDevice's WHERE window tolerates only one minute of future timestamp (updated_at BETWEEN UpdatedAt-30d AND UpdatedAt+1min), so a device row written by an instance whose clock runs more than one minute ahead falls outside the window evaluated on other instances. In a multi-instance deployment with more than one minute of clock skew, an active device last tagged by the fast-clock instance matches 0 rows and is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached once the limit is saturated — a known, working device loses anonymous access while the limit is full.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds updateDevice's success path — a known active device being refreshed when the limit is reached — but the only new test (TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit) exercises the rejection branch, leaving the BETWEEN-window update untested. A regression in the window bounds or WHERE clause (e.g., during the next retention tweak) makes every known device match 0 rows and be rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached once the limit is reached — the exact population the feature must keep working — with no failing test to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The enforcement chain — client.go's errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) matching the error that survives TagDevice → tagDeviceUI → CreateOrUpdateDevice — has no test anywhere in the diff. A lossy error wrap in tagDeviceUI or a refactor at either end of the chain makes errors.Is return false, demoting the limit error to the logged-and-ignored branch so anonymous auth silently succeeds past the configured limit, with no failing test to detect the disabled enforcement.

[ADVISORY] The httpReqCopy machinery (its RemoteAddr restore at lines 41-42) existed so the request could safely outlive the handler inside the deleted goroutine, but TagDevice now runs synchronously before Authenticate returns. Every anonymous request still pays for copying the request and every future reader must puzzle over async-safety code whose justification is gone; deleting the copy and passing r.HTTPRequest directly removes the copy block and the restore.

[ADVISORY] The device limit turns a client-controlled identifier into a global admission gate: device IDs arrive as client-supplied cookies/headers, so any unauthenticated client can register device_limit distinct IDs and lock every new anonymous user out, and the exact cap is published to attackers via the public frontend-settings payload (AnonymousDeviceLimit in getFrontendSettings). An attacker sends device_limit requests with distinct device IDs to an anonymous-enabled instance; CountDevices then reports the cap reached, every first-time or cookie-less visitor's Authenticate returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, and public dashboards serve auth errors to all new anonymous users for up to 30 days — maintainable indefinitely by the attacker re-tagging its fake devices once per month, since there is no per-IP scoping, rate limit, or challenge distinguishing attacker devices from real ones.

[BUG] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the device limit with a non-atomic check-then-act: CountDevices runs in one DB session and the insert runs in a separate session with no transaction, row lock, or constraint arbitrating between them, so concurrent registrations overshoot the configured cap. N concurrent requests with unique device IDs arriving while count sits just below device_limit all observe count < limit and all insert, leaving the device count above the configured maximum; the overshoot never self-corrects because over-limit devices keep refreshing their updated_at through updateDevice, so the licensing/cost cap the feature exists to enforce is permanently violated after a single burst (organic viral traffic or a deliberate race).

[ADVISORY] Authenticate now runs device tagging synchronously on the request context (previously a fire-and-forget goroutine with its own context.Background() and 2-minute timeout), so every uncached anonymous request blocks on a SELECT COUNT over anon_device plus an UPSERT roundtrip before the identity is returned. Anonymous request latency now tracks database health — a slow or saturated DB stalls all anonymous auth instead of merely skipping telemetry — and an attacker sending requests with unique device IDs (bypassing the 29-minute local cache on every request) converts each cheap unauthenticated HTTP request into a COUNT query plus a DB write with no rate limit on the path.

[ADVISORY] The rewrite deletes the recover() that specifically guarded TagDevice panics (the removed code logged "Tag anon session panic", evidence this path panicked in practice), so a panic in tagging now propagates through Authenticate into the live request instead of being contained. Whatever input previously triggered the tagging panic the old code was written to contain now aborts the anonymous request (connection reset / 500) rather than degrading to a warning — a known-panicky path was moved into the request path with its containment removed.

[ADVISORY] The only enforcement point of the device limit — the errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) check in Authenticate — is exercised by no test in the diff: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit stops at the store layer, and the impl tests construct the service with setting.NewCfg() whose AnonymousDeviceLimit is the zero value. The block-on-limit behavior depends on ErrDeviceLimitReached crossing the unmodified tagDeviceUI call chain unwrapped; if that pre-existing function wraps or replaces the error, the check silently falls through to log-and-allow and the limit ships as a no-op — and CI gives no signal because the client-level rejection is never tested.

[BUG] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit exercises only updateDevice's zero-rows rejection branch — it never calls CreateOrUpdateDevice for a device that already exists while the limit is reached — so the feature's core behavior ('if device limit is reached, only update devices') is verified by no test in the diff. The suite stays green with updateDevice semantically broken: an inverted BETWEEN window (updated_at BETWEEN UpdatedAt+1min AND UpdatedAt-30d) or swapped client_ip/user_agent SET args are valid SQL that match zero rows or write wrong values, and the test's sole assertion (require.ErrorIs ErrDeviceLimitReached, database_test.go:69) is satisfied either way; in production that defect makes every returning anonymous device hit ErrDeviceLimitReached, which client.go:44-46 now propagates out of Authenticate, locking out all anonymous access once the limit is reached with zero red tests — the test also cannot distinguish the real gate (count >= deviceLimit) from a broken 'count > 0'. Test files checked: database_test.go (only the rejection case is asserted) and impl_test.go (runs with limit 0).

[ADVISORY] The new TagDevice error-propagation branch (impl.go:147 'return err') is triggered by no test in the diff: the adapted impl_test.go tag tests construct the service with setting.NewCfg(), whose AnonymousDeviceLimit is the zero value 0 — making the limit gate dead code in those tests — and require.NoError on every TagDevice call (impl_test.go:120-121). Deleting the 'return err' or breaking the errors.Is(anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) check in client.go leaves every test in the diff green while the device limit becomes unenforced end-to-end; the enforcement chain has four links (CreateOrUpdateDevice → tagDeviceUI → TagDevice → Anonymous.Authenticate) and the diff verifies only the innermost one (database_test.go:62-69). Test files checked: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go and pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl_test.go — the only test files in this diff touching this behavior.

[BUG] updateDevice's WHERE clause only matches rows whose stored updated_at falls in [device.UpdatedAt-30d, device.UpdatedAt+1min], so an existing device whose last update is older than 30 days matches zero rows and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached — a known returning device is treated identically to an unknown one — and no test in the diff covers this branch. On an instance with auth.anonymous device_limit set and the limit reached by other active devices, an anonymous visitor returning after a 30-day gap fails authentication outright (client.go:44-46 returns the error from Authenticate, producing an error response instead of anonymous access) rather than having their known device refreshed, and stays rejected until the retention job deletes the expired row — the opposite of the code comment 'if device limit is reached, only update devices'; TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit covers only the unknown-device rejection, never the expired-known-device case.

[ADVISORY] ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now hardcodes the concrete store (anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit), impl.go:44) instead of accepting the anonstore.AnonStore interface, and the adapted test reads devices back through the private anonStore field (impl_test.go:124). The store can no longer be substituted through the constructor, so the next contributor testing a store-driven error path (including the ErrDeviceLimitReached propagation this diff adds) must build real DB fixtures or bypass the constructor entirely — friction this diff already pays, since the adapted tests reach into the private field and still achieve zero coverage of the limit path at the service level.

[BUG] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces device_limit with a non-atomic count-then-write: the CountDevices check and the subsequent upsert run in separate database sessions with no transaction, row lock, or constraint tying them together, so concurrent first-time devices each observe count < deviceLimit and each insert. Operators who set auth.anonymous device_limit to cap anonymous device storage find the cap silently exceeded under concurrent load — an unauthenticated client firing parallel requests registers devices past the configured limit, defeating the feature's enforcement purpose.

[ADVISORY] Anonymous.Authenticate now executes TagDevice synchronously on the request context, replacing the fire-and-forget goroutine that ran tagging on context.Background() with a 2-minute timeout and a recover() guard. Every cache-miss anonymous auth (first visit, or roughly every 29 minutes per device per instance behind a load balancer) now blocks on the tagging DB roundtrips, so a slow or connection-exhausted database stalls anonymous page loads that previously proceeded untagged, and a panic in the tagging path now fails the request instead of being absorbed.

[BUG] When the device limit is reached, Authenticate returns the bare anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached sentinel — a plain fmt.Errorf carrying no HTTP status — straight to the authn broker, and nothing in this diff maps it to a defined response. Over-limit anonymous visitors get the broker's generic internal-error handling (a 500-style server error) instead of a defined client error, so the feature's 'reject new devices' behavior surfaces as server errors that inflate error-rate alerts and look like outages.

[ADVISORY] When device_limit > 0, CreateOrUpdateDevice runs CountDevices — a count over the whole anon_device table filtered only by the 30-day updated_at window — before every cache-miss tag, in addition to the write itself. Operators enabling the limit on deployments with large anon_device tables add a per-tag count whose cost scales with the active-device count (the very quantity the limit caps), extending the now-synchronous anonymous auth path and spiking database CPU.

[ADVISORY] The diff declares anonymousDeviceExpiration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour here while an identically-named constant with the same value is also declared in the api package (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go:17), two hand-maintained copies of the window that now drives both limit enforcement and the admin device list. A future maintainer tuning the enforcement window in one package leaves the other stale, so the admin API serves a device list whose time window no longer matches what the device limit counts, and operators inspecting devices see a set that diverges from the cap's actual behavior.

[BUG] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the device limit with a non-transactional count-then-write: CountDevices (line 110) and the subsequent insert run as separate statements with no lock, transaction, or in-flight guard, so concurrent requests that each observe count just below deviceLimit all proceed and insert past the cap. Under the device-flood conditions this limit exists for, N concurrent first-time anonymous requests against a nearly-full limit all pass the count check and all insert, growing anon_device beyond the configured device_limit — the cap the operator set is not enforced exactly when it matters, and the overshoot scales with request concurrency.

[BUG] Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context with no deadline, deleting the detached goroutine that carried the 2-minute timeoutTag, so the anon_device count+write runs unbounded on the anonymous auth critical path. A slow or locked anon_device statement (lock wait, connection-pool exhaustion, stalled network) now stalls every anonymous request that reaches tagging for the driver's full timeout instead of completing off-path capped at 2 minutes — a best-effort telemetry write can now hang or fail anonymous page loads, and client disconnects cancel the tagging mid-write.

[BUG] ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned from the authn client as a bare fmt.Errorf with no HTTP status mapping anywhere in the diff, so the authn middleware's generic error handler determines the response shape over-limit anonymous visitors receive. Once the limit is reached, every new anonymous visitor receives the generic authentication-failure/500-style response instead of a 4xx identifying a device-limit policy rejection — an expected, operator-configured condition is reported as a server-side auth error, misdirecting users and tripping 5xx alerting for a normal policy outcome.

[BUG] updateDevice reassigns the captured args slice inside the WithDbSession callback (args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)), making the callback non-idempotent even though WithDbSession re-invokes callbacks on database connection failover; on the second invocation the query string is already in args and gets prepended again, so Exec binds the SQL text as the first placeholder argument. During any DB failover event the callback runs twice and every updateDevice call fails with a placeholder/argument-count mismatch, so returning anonymous devices silently stop being refreshed (only a Warn log) and devices near the 30-day window edge get rejected as over-limit — the HA rescue path is deterministically broken for this statement.

[ADVISORY] With a limit configured, every device tag performs an unconditional CountDevices range query before the write, and rejected over-limit devices are never added to the local cache (it is only populated on successful tags), so each of their requests repeats the count plus a failing UPDATE synchronously in auth.
